answer:
Create the file case_120.inp in the current working directory containing exactly the input deck provided in the inp code block, preserving all whitespace, line breaks, and content character-for-character.
Run CalculiX in the working directory using the command ccx -i case_120. If that form is not accepted, fall back to ccx case_120.
Capture the standard output and standard error of the ccx invocation for later reporting.
After the solver process finishes, open case_120.sta and scan its contents. If the file contains a line indicating successful termination (for example the string "JOB COMPLETED"), treat the run as successful. Otherwise treat it as failed.
Run ccx -v (or the closest equivalent that prints the version string) in the same working directory and capture the version string printed to stdout.
List all files that CalculiX generated during the run (for example case_120.sta, case_120.frd, case_120.cvg, case_120.dat, case_120.pvd, case_120.msg, or any others that appeared) and record them as strings in a flat JSON array.
Create a file named results.json in the working directory with the following JSON schema and populate every field:
"solver": the string "calculix".
"case_id": the string "case_120".
"status": "success" if the .sta check passed, otherwise "error".
"ccx_version": the version string captured from ccx -v.
"artifacts": the array of generated output file names listed above, or an empty array if none were produced.
"notes": a string that states the exact ccx command that was executed. If the run failed, append the error message or relevant portion of the .sta / .dat / stderr output that indicates the failure, and name the file in which the error was found.
Do not modify the physics, mesh, boundary conditions, material definitions, step definitions, or any other keyword in the input deck. Write the .inp file exactly as supplied.
